verdict.rationale: Airbyte's REST API is documented for programmatic control of syncs (e.g., with orchestrators like Airflow) and the Connection Timeline exposes historical events, errors and logs for diagnosing failed runs, giving an agent a path to check status and diagnose failures via API. An official MCP server exists (docs.airbyte.com/community/mcp-servers) connecting agents like Claude/Cursor to Airbyte, but its documented purpose is querying/acting on synced data rather than exposing sync-management operations (status check, re-trigger) through MCP specifically. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of MCP tools/endpoints for checking sync status or re-triggering a failed sync, and explicit API endpoint documentation for triggering a re-sync (only general 'programmatic interaction' is claimed).
